Question: Why did the Second Temple fall, historically speaking?

Sources:
[0] Berakhot 18b:1 (Berakhot)
בן איש חי אטו כולי עלמא בני מתי נינהו אלא בן איש חי שאפי' במיתתו קרוי חי רב פעלים מקבצאל שריבה וקבץ פועלים לתורה והוא הכה את שני אריאל מואב שלא הניח כמותו לא במקדש ראשון ולא במקדש שני
— 'Son of a living man !' Are there, then, in the whole world sons [born of! dead men ? But, 'son of a living man' [means] even in his death he is called 'living.' 'Of Kabzeel, who had done mighty deeds' — [he is so described] because he multiplied and gathered labourers for the Torah. 'He smote the two altar-hearths of Moab' — i.e. he left nobody like him, neither [in the time of] the first Temple nor the Second Temple. 'He went down also and slew a lion in the midst of a pit in time of snow' — some say :

[1] Berakhot 3b:4 (Berakhot)
מפני המפולת ותיפוק ליה משום חשד ומזיקין
[Why mention] on account of falling fabric, since thou canst derive [a sufficient reason] from the grounds of suspicion and evil spirits ?

[2] Berakhot 58b:4 (Berakhot)
אמר ליה הכי אמר ר' יוחנן מיום שחרב בית המקדש נגזרה גזירה על בתיהן של צדיקים שיחרבו שנאמר (ישעיהו ה, ט) באזני ה' צבאות אם לא בתים רבים לשמה יהיו גדולים וטובים מאין יושב ואמר ר' יוחנן עתיד הקדוש ברוך הוא להחזירן לישובן שנאמר (תהלים קכה, א) שיר המעלות לדוד הבוטחים ביי' כהר ציון מה הר ציון עתיד הקדוש ברוך הוא להחזירו לישובו אף בתיהן של צדיקים עתיד הקב"ה להחזירן לישובן חזייה דלא מיישב דעתיה א"ל דיו לעבד שיהא כרבו
He said to him, "Thus spake R. Johanan : From the day the Temple was destroyed, a decree was issued that the houses of the righteous should be destroyed ; as it is said, 'In mine ears said the Lord of hosts : Of a truth many houses shall be desolate, even great and fair, without inhabitant' (Is. v. 9). Also said R. Johanan: The Holy One, blessed be He, will restore them to habitation ; as it is said, 'A Song of Ascents. They that trust in the Lord are as Mount Zion' (Ps. cxxv. 1) — just as the Holy One, blessed be He, will restore Mount Zion to habitation, so will He restore the houses of the righteous to habitation." He perceived that his mind was still not at rest, so he said to him, "It is enough for the slave to be like his master."

[3] Numbers 16:31 (Numbers)
וַיְהִי֙ כְּכַלֹּת֔וֹ לְדַבֵּ֕ר אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַתִּבָּקַ֥ע הָאֲדָמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּחְתֵּיהֶֽם׃
And it came to pass, as he made an end of speaking all these words, that the ground did cleave asunder that was under them.

[4] Berakhot 3a:15 (Berakhot)
תנו רבנן מפני שלשה דברים אין נכנסין לחורבה מפני חשד מפני המפולת ומפני המזיקין. מפני חשד ותיפוק ליה משום מפולת
Our Rabbis have taught : For three reasons one should not enter ruins : on account of suspicion, of falling fabric and evil spirits. [Why mention] on account of suspicion, since thou canst derive [a sufficient reason] from the danger of falling fabric ?

[5] Berakhot 12a:6 (Berakhot)
תניא נמי הכי ר' נתן אומר בגבולין בקשו לקרות כן אלא שכבר בטלום מפני תרעומת המינין
There is a teaching to the same effect : R. Nathan said : Outside the Temple they wished to read [the Decalogue with the Shema'] but it had long been abolished because of the murmuring of the Minim.

[6] Berakhot 32a:27 (Berakhot)
(במדבר יד, טז) מבלתי יכולת ה' יכול ה' מיבעי ליה
"Because the Lord was not able [yekolet]" (Num. xiv. 16). It should have been yakol!

[7] Mishneh Torah, Prayer and the Priestly Blessing 5:14 (Mishneh Torah, Prayer and the Priestly Blessing)
כשהוא עושה נפילת פנים אחר תפלה יש מי שהוא עושה קידה ויש מי שהוא עושה השתחויה ואסור לעשות השתחויה על האבנים אלא במקדש כמו שבארנו בהל' עבודת כוכבים ואין אדם חשוב רשאי ליפול על פניו אא"כ הוא יודע בעצמו שהוא צדיק כיהושע אבל מטה פניו מעט ואינו כובש אותן בקרקע ומותר לאדם להתפלל במקום זה וליפול על פניו במקום אחר.
When performing the rite of "falling on the face", after the service, some fall on the face, some prostrate themselves. The latter is forbidden on a stone floor, except in the Temple of Jerusalem, as has been explained in the laws concerning Idolatry. [Even] a worthy person may not fall on his face unless he is conscious that he is a righteous man like Joshua. He should only incline his face somewhat, but not press it against the floor. It is permissible to recite the service of prayer in one spot and "fall upon the face" elsewhere.

Answer segments:
(0) sources=[]: **The sources provided don't answer this question.** None of them explains why the Second Temple was destroyed, either historically (political or military causes) or in the rabbinic sense of what sins led to it. I won't answer from memory.

The texts here mention the Temple only in passing:

- **Berakhot 58b** speaks of what followed the destruction, not what caused it. Rabbi Yochanan teaches: 
(1) sources=[2]: "From the day the Temple was destroyed, a decree was issued that the houses of the righteous should be destroyed"
(2) sources=[]: . He adds a consolation: 
(3) sources=[2]: "just as the Holy One, blessed be He, will restore Mount Zion to habitation, so will He restore the houses of the righteous to habitation."
(4) sources=[]:  When this did not calm his listener, he said, 
(5) sources=[2]: "It is enough for the slave to be like his master."
(6) sources=[]: 
- **Berakhot 18b** uses both Temples only as a measure of greatness. It says Benayahu 
(7) sources=[0]: left nobody like him, neither [in the time of] the first Temple nor the Second Temple.
(8) sources=[]: 
- **Berakhot 12a** contrasts practice 
(9) sources=[5]: outside the Temple
(10) sources=[]:  with practice inside it, but says nothing about the destruction.

For the historical question, you'd want historical sources on the Roman period. For the rabbinic explanations of the Churban, you'd need the relevant Talmudic passages added to our study set. I'd be glad to study them with you once they're provided.
